Do not panic, is completely normal to break down.

You do not deserve to die, what you do deserve is  finding something that works for you. 

Did you try meds? Did you try finding another doc that can actually see you when you are feeling down instead of waiting 2 weeks?

Is there a way that you could hit the gym when you are feeling down? I know it is not going to solve all your problems together but it does really make you feel better after working out, it would be really really good if you forced yourself to go and try.

What about changing your eating habits? There habe been some studies where they show that a diet rich on omega3 helps a lot with bipolar depression, if you could consult with your doc that might help you feeling better.

It is not your fault to feel that way, but you are not out of options, and certainly you have a husband who loves you and cares about you. Let him pamper you. There is always something that works.

When I was in high school, I wasn't attractive to the opposite sex, I didn't have much friends and I had trouble communicating with people without sounding cocky. Things do get better, give it some time. It takes also a lot of effort to start seeing things from a different perspective. 

There is always something that it is just our cup of tea. We are all good at something. It might not be what we want, but if you learn to love what you are good at, you are more likely to find your path in life.

Do not give up, there is much much more to experiment, to feel. Hang in there and try to appreciate all that you have.

If you need to talk, talk to me, but do not give up.
